thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager: GeoDNS / external resolver errors detected for EU region. Route53 health checks flapping; Cloudflare returning 5xx for a subset of edges. Automated routing failovers triggered but some customers still reporting errors. Runbook: geodns/resolver-outage. Please ack and join #incidents.

Alice Chen: acked. I'm oncall for infra this shift. starting triage.

Raj Patel: joining. grabbing resolver logs and Route53 console now. do we have a list of impacted prefixes/ASNs?

Tim Wu: I see increased NXDOMAIN and SERVFAIL counts from our EU resolver pool 10.2.0.0/24 -> upstream Cloudflare resolvers showing 5xx timeouts around 08:12 UTC.

Maria Gomez: Support is seeing ~40 tickets for errors: "upstream error, try later" and some customers in FR/DE complaining about failed embeddings. Escalated a couple for enterprise SLAs.

Sophia Lee: what's the customer impact surface? Is this affecting hosted API only or also Dedicated/Private?

Raj Patel: initial check: mostly Hosted API traffic from EU regions hitting our edge resolvers. Dedicated customers with VPC endpoints look fine. Private on-prem unaffected.

Alice Chen: good. plan: 1) fail traffic off primary EU geodns record to EU-2 secondary 2) reduce TTL to 60 to speed propagation 3) open comms. Need owners for each step.

Tim Wu: taking step 1/2. I'm going to apply a Route53 traffic policy change (manual failover) and update TTL. Will post commands and outputs.

Tim Wu: applying change now.
```bash
# set failover routing policy: primary -> eu-1, secondary -> eu-2
aws route53 change-resource-record-sets --hosted-zone-id Z123EXAMPLE --change-batch file://failover-eu.json
# change TTL for primary record
aws route53 change-resource-record-sets --hosted-zone-id Z123EXAMPLE --change-batch '{"Changes":[{"Action":"UPSERT","ResourceRecordSet":{"Name":"api.redwood.example","Type":"A","TTL":60,"SetIdentifier":"primary-eu","Weight":0,"Region":"eu-west-1","ResourceRecords":[{"Value":"3.4.5.6"}]}}]}'
```

Tim Wu: Route53 change submitted. Change ID: C000EXAMPLE. Propagation check in progress.

Raj Patel: I'm opening a support ticket with Cloudflare to confirm edge behavior and whether there is a known resolver outage. Also spinning up extra resolver instances in eu-west-1 to handle retry storms.

incident-bot: Automated note: health check eu-primary-api-health reports UNHEALTHY -> last failed check at 08:13:21 UTC. Automatic failover attempted at 08:14:05 UTC.

Maria Gomez: Publishing status page draft now: "We are investigating intermittent DNS resolution failures impacting some EU customers. Engineers are actively working on routing changes and upstream provider coordination." Any ETA?

Sophia Lee: aim for initial customer comms within 15m. Once failover completes confirm error reduction, then update.

Tim Wu: Route53 change is in sync across most endpoints, I see traffic shifting to eu-2. TTL change applied.

Raj Patel: Cloudflare support responded: they're seeing elevated 5xx from a subset of their EU edges due to an internal config push. They've acknowledged and are rolling back. No ETA given yet.

Alice Chen: good. keep monitor. Raj, own post-mortem for provider coordination. Tim, monitor resolver CPU/queues; if retry queue grows we may need to enable rate-limiting on our ingress. Maria, push status update after next check.

Tim Wu: monitoring: client error rate down ~70% for EU region after failover. Some residual errors for sessions pinned to old DNS entries (clients honoring TTL).

Maria Gomez: status page update posted: "Mitigation in progress: traffic being routed to alternate EU region. We will post updates every 30 minutes." Link: https://status.redwood.example/incidents/1951234567

incident-bot: :bell: Paging Raj Patel for next on-call rotation in 20 minutes per schedule.

Alice Chen: I'm handing oncall to Raj in 20. Raj if you need a full handoff doc it's in /runbooks/geodns-outage.md.

Raj Patel: taking handoff at 08:40 UTC. I'll continue monitoring Cloudflare ticket and our resolver fleet. Setting up a 30-minute follow-up call with networking and support.

Tim Wu: note for post-mortem: consider lowering default TTL for geo A records during peak deploy windows, and improve our automated fallback so failover propagates even with client-side caching.

Maria Gomez: collecting impacted customer list for outreach. Starting targeted emails to enterprise customers affected.

Sophia Lee: thanks team. keep thread updated. we may want to include SLA impact calc in the post-incident summary.

Raj Patel: Cloudflare confirmed rollback complete at 08:53 UTC. I'm seeing resolvers stable and 5xx metrics back to baseline. Will keep failover in place for another hour then consider switching back after monitoring.

Tim Wu: agree. leaving failover until 10:00 UTC. keeping TTL at 60 for now.

incident-bot: Incident update: mitigated -> monitoring. Incident ticket INC-1951234567 created.

Alice Chen: thanks all. handing off officially to Raj. I'm now offline for the next break.

Raj Patel: taking over. I'll run the 1-hour checks and then coordinate rollback once metrics are clean.

oncall-notifications-bot: Reminder: scheduled postmortem meeting created: 2025-04-03T15:00:00Z in #postmortems. Organizer: Raj Patel.

Sophia Lee: adding action items: provider comms play refinement, improve failover automation, update support templates.

Maria Gomez: closing loop with customers who were flagged as impacted. will attach timeline to INC ticket.

Alice Chen: good work everyone.
